newsitem.title: CHINA: Chirac, China's leaders to issue joint communique.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, China's leaders to issue joint communique.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac will visit China this week and issue a joint communique with Chinese leaders stating their desire and determination to strengthen ties, a Chinese government spokesman said on Tuesday.
Chirac is scheduled to visit China May 15-18, when he is expected to announce new business deals worth millions of dollars, Chinese officials and Western diplomats said.
"Our leaders and President Chirac...will issue a joint communique expounding their view of the international situation," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing in Beijing.
The communique would also state their "desire and determination to further strengthen Sino-French ties", Shen said. He gave no further details of the communique.

Sino-French relations soured in the early 1990s over sales of French jet fighters and frigates to China's rival, Taiwan, but have recovered since Paris pledged in 1994 to end arms sales to the island, which Beijing considers a rebel province.

In an interview with the French magazine Politique Internationale carried on Monday by the French daily Le Figaro, China's President Jiang Zemin said Chirac's visit would give relations a new momentum in all fields.
Shen, the ministry spokesman, said Chirac's trip would "achieve substantive results both politically and economically". He did not elaborate.
Chirac was expected to make strong overtures in favour of French industries, including arms manufacturers, during his visit, his aides have said.
Airbus Industrie is hoping Chirac's visit would clinch orders for up to 100 airliners worth $4 billion for the European consortium.

Chirac's visit had accelerated negotiations on a $20 million venture between France's Elf Atochem, the chemicals unit of Elf Aquitaine, and China's Wuhan Organic Chemical Industry Co that would produce benzyl chloride and phenyl acetic acid.
The trip had also hastened approval for the creation of a China holding company for Elf Atochem that would provide services for the French firm's Chinese joint ventures.
Shen said Chirac's trip would have important significance to future Sino-French relations and a far-reaching impact on the world. He did not elaborate.
Accompanied by his wife Bernadette and several senior ministers, Chirac was also scheduled to visit Shanghai, where a French trade exhibition would open.
Chirac was visiting despite the May 25-June 1 snap parliamentary election at home. However, he has dropped a planned stopover in Hong Kong due to election campaigning.
Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng visited France last year and parliament chief Qiao Shi met Chirac in Paris on March 27.
